current_text.html:
BCO 7-1

Under the New Testament, our Lord at first collected His people out of different nations, and united them to the household of faith by the ministry of extraordinary officers who received extraordinary gifts of the Spirit and who were agents by whom God completed His revelation to His Church. Such officers and gifts related to new revelation have no successors since God completed His revelation at the conclusion of the Apostolic Age.

BCO 7-2

The ordinary and perpetual classes of office in the Church are elders and deacons. Within the class of elder are the two orders of teaching elders and ruling elders. The elders jointly have the government and spiritual oversight of the Church, including teaching. Only those elders who are specially gifted, called and trained by God to preach may serve as teaching elders. The office of deacon is not one of rule, but rather of service both to the physical and spiritual needs of the people. In accord with Scripture, these offices are open to men only.

BCO 7-3

No one who holds office in the Church ought to usurp authority therein, or receive any official titles of spiritual preeminence, except such as are employed in the Scriptures. Furthermore, unordained people shall not be referred to as, or given the titles of, the ordained offices of pastor/elder, or deacon.

relationships.title: BCO 7 qualifications limited to biological men who hold office

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found that an overture amending BCO 7 regarding the requirement that church officers be men is not in conflict with the BCO.

relationships.title: Codifying biblical sexuality standard for church officers in BCO 7

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found that amending BCO 7 to codify the biblical standard for church officers related to human sexuality is not in conflict with the BCO.

relationships.title: Officers' self-identification by biblical sins barred in BCO 7

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found that amending BCO 7 to prohibit church officers from self-describing by biblical sins (e.g., 'gay Christian') is not in conflict with the BCO.

relationships.title: Disqualifying from office men who identify as homosexual
relationships.disposition: not in conflict; Adopted by the CCB

occurrences.excerpt: CCB found no constitutional conflict in an overture to amend BCO 7 disqualifying from ordained office men who identify as homosexual.

relationships.title: Disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination under BCO 7

occurrences.excerpt: An overture from Westminster Presbytery to amend BCO 7 and related provisions disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination was found in conflict and adopted.
